$comment: EXAMPLE CBOM. Intended NOT to conform to pkic.example.pqc-migration v0.7 (draft). Identical to cbom-keycloak-pqc-pass except that the storage interface sto-realm-keys omits keyWrappingSupported, so it fails pqc-migration#I12, new in v0.7, and nothing else. Omitting moduleValidationScheme (I10) does not isolate: I11's guard holds when the scheme is absent, so I11 fails with it. Worked example built from cprofile/Linux_Keycloak_26.7.3_cprofile.json (corrected 27 September 2026) and the sources in drafts/pqc-migration-depths/examples-keycloak-plan.md. Subject is the container image (decision 0022, K1). Transport and security protocols are cryptographic-asset protocol components. Every application protocol is a CycloneDX service, HTTPS included; every protocol component is a TLS instance (K7). A service that applies cryptography of its own (OIDC, SAML, the Admin API, brokered token verification) or has no transport protection (plain HTTP) is an interface and carries pkic:profile:interfaceType. A service that only rides TLS (HTTPS, JDBC, LDAP, SMTP, JGroups) is declared for its layering and carries no interface attributes; the TLS component under it is the interface. Layering is the dependency graph: OIDC depends on HTTPS, HTTPS on TLS; plain HTTP depends on nothing. 'none' states that no algorithm is applied for a job (K3). Implementation facts are stated once on the library that provides an interface and inherited by it (K9): module validation, provider location, enablement method, coexistence and capability by purpose. An interface states a value only where it differs, and a capability entry for one purpose replaces the provider's entry for that purpose. Each distinct TLS configuration is one protocol component without interfaceType, which the TLS interfaces reference through relatedCryptographicAssets. Native CycloneDX fields carry what they can (see drafts/pqc-migration-depths/mapping-native-fields-review.md): the implementing library by dependencies[].provides, provider location by executionEnvironment, supported TLS groups and signature schemes by cipherSuites (which list the supported set, while cryptoRefArray lists what is in use), key types, formats and wrapping by related-crypto-material components and their securedBy, and interface-set completeness by compositions. Attributes with no CycloneDX field are pkic:profile: properties. The companion SBOM reference is an illustrative BOM-Link. To verify before publication: the JDK update in the image; the SAML, cluster-transport and brokered-verification capability status; the JEP 527 backport status for the Red Hat build of JDK 21; productCertificationScheme for upstream Keycloak.
